newsitem.title: USA: NAPM report shows manufacturing slowed in October.
newsitem.headline: NAPM report shows manufacturing slowed in October.

text.p: The U.S. manufacturing sector grew more slowly in October than in September, according to a survey of the nation's purchasing executives released Friday.

The National Association of Purchasing Management said its monthly index fell to 50.2 percent in October from 51.7 percent in September. A reading above 50 indicates the manufacturing economy is generally expanding, while one below 50 indicates contraction.
The NAPM surveys more than 300 purchasing executives monthly to obtain their assessment of the economy.
The group cited declines in reported new orders, order backlogs, inventories and employment for the drop in the overall index.

"Purchasing executives' comments on business conditions in October included more remarks such as 'slowing' and 'orders down' than those indicating 'business good' or 'strong,'" said Ralph Kauffman, chair of the group's business survey committee, in a statement accompanying the survey.
On Wall Street, economists reacted favourably to the report, which appeared to show the economy continuing to grow at a healthy pace with little inflation.

"I think it's just one more piece of information suggesting that the economy has moderated to a more sustainable pace and that strains on resources remain dormant right now," said Joshua Feinman, global markets economist at Bankers Trust.

NAPM said the prices paid component of the survey fell to 47.1 percent in October from 51.2 in September. The new orders index fell to 51.6 percent from 56.3 and inventories dropped to 38.9 percent from 44.8.
The data suggest a modest rally in the industrial sector over the last few months may be cooling, Kauffman told reporters in a teleconference after the report's release.
"Overall, there was certainly an upsurge (previously) and now there seems to be some tapering off. That tapering off is showing itself now," Kauffman said.
On the positive side, manufacturers' production expanded for the seventh consecutive month in October, with the production component of the NAPM index rising to 56.6 percent from 54.1.
The production index peaked at 57.0 in August, which was its highest level since 59.9 in January 1995.
